claims.statement: Three deep-agent graphs are registered in langgraph.json: `reviewer` (`agent.graphs.reviewer:traced_reviewer_agent`), `analyzer` (`agent.graphs.analyzer:traced_analyzer`), and `review-scout` (`agent.graphs.review_scout:traced_review_scout`).

get_reviewer_agent builds the reviewer deep agent per run with a reviewer-only toolset (fetch_review_diff, add_finding, update_finding, list_findings, publish_review, resolve_finding_thread, reply_to_finding_thread plus read helpers), returning an empty agent when there is no thread_id or the graph is not loaded for execution.
get_reviewer_agent copies the incoming config before mutating it so it does not clobber the caller's recursion_limit.

The reviewer configures a single reviewer subagent that reviews an explicit disjoint file partition and returns candidate defects only; the subagent cannot call finding or publication tools and the parent validates, records, and publishes.

PrepareReviewerRunMiddleware performs deterministic non-LLM setup before the first model call: it ensures the sandbox, mints and caches a repo-scoped GitHub App installation token as a bot token, and clones-or-fetches plus force-checks-out the PR head via prepare_review_repo.

The reviewer computes a unified diff and the set of in-diff (file, line) tuples during run prep and passes both as diff_text and diff_line_set in run state so add_finding can validate at creation time rather than at GitHub-publish time.

The reviewer run prep gathers context concurrently including PR title/body, existing PR review threads, the learned repo-style prompt, org guidelines, root and scoped AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md from the base ref, an API-standards skill, approval policy, and an optional scout walkthrough.

Author-controlled inputs (PR title/body, existing review-thread comments, finding replies, and walkthrough text) are wrapped in XML data blocks whose closing tags are neutralized by _escape_for_data_block and whose logins are validated against the GitHub username grammar.
Findings live in PostgreSQL under the pull request; reviewer thread metadata retains thread-level PR state, and first access migrates legacy metadata findings once.

The Finding TypedDict records severity, confidence, category, title, file plus start/end line and side, in_diff, description, optional suggestion, status, first_seen/last_confirmed SHAs, GitHub comment/thread/resolved-thread id lists, surface_state, human-reply bookkeeping, diff_hunk, a content fingerprint, interactions, and rank.

add_finding rejects any finding whose start_line..end_line range is not part of the PR diff, returning success:false with in_diff:false so the model does not re-anchor or retry; out-of-diff findings are disabled.

publish_review batches eligible open, in-diff findings above the severity threshold (default medium, capped at REVIEW_FINDING_CAP) into one GitHub PR Review with one inline comment per renderable finding, appending a fenced suggestion block when present.
Each published inline comment embeds an open-swe-review-comment JSON marker so later runs can re-locate the finding's GitHub thread by finding id.

reconcile_findings_with_review_threads syncs tracked findings against current GitHub review-thread state before each run: it records new comment/thread ids and marks findings surfaced, folds a finding to resolved when all its threads are resolved, and captures the latest human reply as a needs_reassessment interaction with a reconciliation note.

The reviewer opts into allow_replacement=True for its sandbox because the sandbox holds only a checkout re-derived each run and durable findings live outside the sandbox; only when replacement also fails does the run die with a typed on-PR notification.

The analyzer graph learns a per-repo review-style prompt for the reviewer by mining historical human PR review feedback and the reviewer's own past finding outcomes, using a sandbox GitHub proxy for the target repository.

Analyzer playbooks are served to the deepagents SkillsMiddleware as virtual files via a StateBackend mounted at the /skills/ route in a CompositeBackend, seeded into the run input files channel by build_skill_files, so nothing is written to the execution sandbox.

The analyzer's save_review_style_prompt tool persists the synthesized custom_prompt plus summary, reviewers, and counts to the REVIEW_STYLES store keyed by review_style_full_name and marks the record completed.

On a successful save_review_style_prompt, ensure_continual_cron idempotently registers one daily LangGraph continual-learning cron per repo, staggered by a hash of the repo name across 05:00-08:59 UTC.

The nightly continual cron is threadless but its configurable pins the repo's deterministic review_style_thread_id, because otherwise get_analyzer would early-return an empty agent and no-op; the threadless run carries no message history so runs do not accumulate across nights.

ReviewStyle records are stored in the typed `review_styles` namespace and track analysis status, prompt and sampling metadata, analysis thread/run identifiers, cron identifier, error, and timestamps; reviewer prompt lookup fails soft if this store is unavailable.

Bootstrap analysis collects samples before creating a durable analyzer run and marks the style record failed if collection or run startup fails; an immediate continual run uses the same deterministic review-style thread.

The review scout runs on a dedicated deterministic PR thread, prepares a replaceable App-authenticated sandbox, resets the PR head diff onto its merge base, and exposes only walkthrough-step and human-input tools.

A ReviewScoutTarget reuses a walkthrough only for its exact PR head, joins an already active run for that head, otherwise starts a durable review-scout run, and makes the reviewer fall back without walkthrough context after 600 seconds or failure.

The scout finalization makes the last intermediate commit tree match the PR head, attributes changed added and deleted lines using blame reconciled to the PR diff, and consolidates unowned or residual work into an Other changes step.

A successful scout replaces the PostgreSQL walkthrough for the PR and head with ordered steps, their added/deleted line ranges, merge base, scout thread, and human-input summary; the reviewer only uses a walkthrough matching its current head.
